about: Chord-fit measurements of the unprocessed sung melody of v2_2 for harmony designer B ('serbest': I ii iii IV V V7 vi, keys C F G). All shares are fractions of the voiced sung time (44.85 s = 8970 frames of 5 ms in the kept syllables of 7 verses), evaluated at each frame's own time in the new song form (placement shifts of kesim.json, no time-stretch).

metric_definitions.chord_tone: sung pitch class is a chord tone of the chord on that beat
metric_definitions.scale_non_chord: in the key's scale but not a chord tone
metric_definitions.outside_scale: not in the key's scale (and not a chord tone); chord_tone + scale_non_chord + outside_scale = 1
metric_definitions.clash_any: not a chord tone AND (a semitone above or below a chord tone OR a tritone from the chord root)
metric_definitions.clash_sustained: the part of clash_any inside a clash run longer than 150 ms; a run survives up to 60 ms without sung pitch (a consonant) and up to 15 ms of non-clash frames; run length = last - first frame + 5 ms
metric_definitions.clash_sustained_strict: same without any bridging (consecutive 5 ms frames only)
metric_definitions.consonant_non_chord: scale_non_chord that is not a clash
metric_definitions.on_beat_chord_tone: chord-tone share of the syllables that start ON a beat (the metrically strong notes)
metric_definitions.off_beat_chord_tone: chord-tone share of the syllables on half beats and sixteenths
metric_definitions.line_end_chord_tone: chord-tone share of the last syllable of each line (the note the phrase rests on)
metric_definitions.sounding_semitone: PHYSICAL, from the band model (bant.py; its I / IV / V7 part is checked note for note against midi/altyapi_C.mid, the ii / iii / vi / V voicings are proposals of designer B): share of the sung time during which a band note one semitone away in pitch class is really sounding (note-on .. note-off + 30 ms)
metric_definitions.sounding_semitone_sustained: the part of sounding_semitone in runs longer than 150 ms
metric_definitions.semitone_same_octave: the same for a band note exactly one semitone above or below the sung note (same octave)
metric_definitions.whole_tone_same_octave: band model: a band note exactly two semitones above or below the sung note is sounding (a major second against the voice)
metric_definitions.band_same_pitch_class: band model: a band note of the sung pitch class is sounding (the voice is doubled by the band)
metric_definitions.band_unison: band model: a band note of exactly the sung pitch is sounding
metric_definitions.J: ranking score = chord_tone - 2 * (clash_sustained + outside_scale) (the same score designer A uses)
metric_definitions.V_and_V7: V = the dominant triad (the band plays no seventh; a sung F is then a non-chord tone that rubs nothing), V7 = with the seventh (a sung F is a chord tone, a sung E lies a semitone below it)
metric_definitions.readings: 'note' (primary): a frame carries the pitch class of the note it belongs to (kesim.json syllable.notes; scoops and glides count with their note). 'frame': every 5 ms frame is rounded on its own. 'dio': the same with a second pitch tracker. 'chords_40ms_early': note mode with all chord changes 40 ms earlier.

rule_sets.strict: G1-G4 of kod/kurallar.py (the dominant only goes to the tonic)
rule_sets.turnaround: the same, but the plain V may step down to IV when that IV goes straight to I (V - IV - I)
rule_sets.any sequence: no rule at all (only to show what the rules cost)

reference_original_d_minor_loop.scale: D natural minor + C# (the leading tone inside the A chord)
reference_original_d_minor_loop.note_on_reading: chord-level metrics only (the original band is not the oom-pah band, so no 'sounding' numbers). tempo.json notes that the A chord of the original has a weak third and a D on top in its last beat; against a plain A major triad the sung D of 'var' / 'Baba'nin' counts as a clash here.

key_ranking_weight_robustness.about: score and bars of the best plan per key for weights w = 1, 2, 4 in J = chord_tone - w * (clash_sustained + outside_scale)

bar_0_verse_opening.about: frames of line 1 only; band_model_beats_0_1 = what sounds against the voice up to beat 1.95 ('Ali Baba'nin')

gliding_syllable_li.what: 2nd syllable of line 1 ('li' of 'Ali'), all 7 verses; kesim.json files it as ONE note G4 with a glide of +2.5 semitones
gliding_syllable_li.reading: the voice holds G4 from about beat 0.52 to 0.75 (while the band's off-beat strum sounds, 0.50-0.78) and is on A4 from about beat 0.78, a sixteenth before the A4 of 'Baba'nin'. Note mode counts the whole syllable as G; frame mode counts only the frames that are really within 50 cents of G.

stage_2_seventh_of_the_dominant.about: bars 2 (L2) and 6 (L4): the dominant with or without its seventh, measured on the frames of that line; the other bars as in the chosen plan. beat_3_only = the frames of beat 3 of that bar.

robustness_of_the_choice.how_to_read: For each reading the best sequence inside the rule set is searched again (J on the frames of that bar's line, ties as in 03_tara.py). 'same harmony as chosen': strict rules: bar 0 = ii ii I I; turnaround rules: bar 0 = V IV I I; both: bar 5 = I I, bars 2 and 6 = the dominant on all four beats (V or V7 on each beat; whether the band plays the seventh is stage 2). J_deficit = J of the reading's pick minus J of the chosen sequence in the same reading (0 = the chosen sequence is the pick). For bars 2 and 6 the deficit of the chosen V V V V is mostly the stage-2 question (a sung F counts as a chord tone only when the symbol is V7); J_deficit_of_the_best_dominant_only_sequence shows what the HARMONY 'dominant on all four beats' loses against the reading's pick (0 in 16 of 18 readings).

bar_2_per_verse.about: do the animal words need different chords? Best sequence inside the strict rules for each verse alone, and the chosen bar per verse

tune_under_the_voice.what: the soft Old MacDonald tune of the existing builder (clarinet C5 C5 C5 G4 A4 A4 G4 in bars 0, 2, 6; repeated C5 on beats 2-3 of bar 5)
tune_under_the_voice.note: voice against tune: shares of the voiced sung time (note mode). tune against chords: share of the tune's own sounding time; clash = a semitone from a chord tone or a tritone from the root.

one_semitone_from_a_sounding_note.note: band model (note-on .. note-off + 30 ms) plus, for the pad rows, the pad's pitch classes held through every sung beat; shares of the voiced sung time, note mode unless marked

optional_voicing_refinements_band_model.about: chosen plan; what sounds against the voice with two optional changes of the strum pattern (rendered-audio numbers: ses_olcumu.json)
